label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's a draft. Fill in the brackets (your name, the date, Darlene's last name) before you hand it in.

---

[Date]

Mrs. Okafor
[Address, or "Delivered via the Transportation Office"]

Re: Your complaint dated October 29, 2026
Bus 41, Route 9, afternoon run, Tuesday, October 27, 2026
Student: Amara Okafor, Fairmont Elementary

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

My name is [Your Name], and I am the driver of Bus 41. My supervisor, Darlene [Last Name], gave me a copy of your complaint on November 3 and asked me to put my account in writing. I am writing it to you directly because you deserve to hear from me, and because I still drive Amara every day and want to get this right with you.

First, I am sorry that Amara and you had such a bad afternoon. I have grandchildren of my own, and I know how frightening it must have been to hear that your daughter was not let off where you expected her. I understand why you were upset.

I also want you to know exactly what happened from where I sat, and why I did what I did.

**What happened**

On the afternoon of October 27, I arrived at the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at 3:52. The schedule has us there at 3:50. Amara is a kindergarten student, and she has the green tag on her bag. That tag means an adult must be at the stop before she can be released from the bus.

I waited until about 3:55. I looked over the corner and the sidewalks, and I did not see an adult there for Amara.

District policy for kindergarten riders is clear. If no adult is at the stop, the student stays on the bus and is returned to school, and the school office calls the parent. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch called the school to let them know Amara was coming back. I had three more stops to make and 14 students still on the bus, so I continued my route.

I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary at 4:31. I walked her into the office myself and handed her to Mrs. Petrakis.

**How Amara was**

Amara was fine the whole time. She was coloring on her folder and was calm and cheerful. At one point she asked if she could ride more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip, and she was happy with that. I did not want her to be frightened, and I made sure she was not.

**About what you saw**

I understand you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and that you waved at the bus. I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, and I did not see you or your car. I am not saying this to blame you. I only want you to know that if I had seen you, I would have known an adult was there, and this would have gone very differently. I would not have ignored someone waving at me.

I cannot get off the bus and walk across the street to look around, because I cannot leave 14 children alone on a bus. That is part of why the rule exists. The driver has to be able to see the adult at the stop from the driver's seat.

You also told the office that I "drove off laughing." I was not laughing. As we pulled away from the stop, I was telling a fourth grader in seat 2 to sit back down. I understand how it may have looked from across the street, and I am sorry it looked that way, but it was not what was happening. I would never laugh at a parent who was worried about her child.

**Why I followed the rule**

I will be honest with you. I am not going to apologize for following the policy, because it is there to protect children like Amara. If I let a kindergartner off with no adult I can see waiting for her, and something happened, I could not forgive myself. I did what I am required to do, and I did it carefully, and I made sure the school and dispatch knew where she was the whole time.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years and have never had a write-up. One other time, years ago on my route, a family went through the same thing with a different child, and they thanked me afterward. I mention it only because I know it is hard to hear this when you are the one waiting at the curb, and I do not take that lightly.

**Camera footage**

Bus 41 has a camera, and it should show the stop and the corner as I saw it that afternoon. I am asking the Transportation Office to pull the footage from October 27, from about 3:50 to 3:56, and to review it. I want it in the file. I have nothing to hide, and I think it will help everyone see what I could and could not see from the driver's seat.

**Going forward**

I would like to make sure this does not happen again, for your sake and for Amara's. I have one request, and I ask it respectfully. When you are picking Amara up, please stand on the same side of the street as the stop, where I can see you from the bus door. If that is not possible, please step out of your car so that I can see you. A wave from inside a parked car across the street is easy to miss, especially with trucks and other vehicles parked along the road. If I can see you, Amara will get off the bus.

I am glad to keep driving Amara. She is a sweet girl, and I look forward to seeing her each afternoon. If you would like to talk with me, I am happy to do that through Darlene or the Transportation Office.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
Bus Driver, Bus 41
[Phone or employee ID, if the office wants it]

cc: Darlene [Last Name], Transportation Supervisor
Employee file

---

A couple of notes:

- I kept to the facts you gave me and didn't add anything about what the policy is called or its number. If you know the policy number, adding it in the "Why I followed the rule" section would help for the file.
- The "years ago, they thanked me" line is optional. If you think it could come across as comparing her to someone else, take it out. The statement works fine without it.
- It's due Friday, November 13, so you have a couple of days. Read it through once and change any wording that doesn't sound like you.
